script: I paid my sister sixteen thousand three hundred dollars to store our mother's furniture, and last March I found out she sold all of it in 2021. Every January she sent me a photo of the unit. It was the same photo. Same boxes, same green sofa, same dust. Four years, one photograph. Three hundred and forty dollars a month, and I have every transfer. Mom died in June 2020. Neither of us could face the house, so my sister put everything in storage. Don't worry about it, she said. I'll handle the paperwork, you handle the money. That seemed fair. She was three hours away, I was the one with a job. She never once asked me for money for the funeral. I took that as her being kind. Then in 2022 it went to three sixty five. She said the facility had raised its rates, and I did not check. In March my wife asked me, completely casually, what the unit number was, and I did not know it, and I realised at my own kitchen table that I had never once known it in four years. I called the facility. They had no unit under her name. They never had. I drove three hours that weekend with the transfers printed out, in a folder, on her kitchen table. I said, tell me where the furniture is. She did not lie. That is the part I keep going back to. She just sat down and said, it's gone, I sold it in 2021. I asked what she did with sixteen thousand dollars. She said, nine hundred of it was the furniture. Then she went to the drawer where our mother kept her coupons and put a receipt in front of me. Fourteen thousand two hundred dollars. A headstone, granite, the plot fee, and four years of maintenance, paid in full, in 2021. I never asked if there was a headstone. Not once in four years. I never went. I asked her why she did not just tell me. And she said, because you would have paid half. She never sent me a bill for that one. She only ever sent me the one for the storage.
